body: Large language models (LLMs) have been ex- ploited to generate malware, but the effective- ness of guardrails for code generation secu- rity remains unclear. We introduce CS-Guard, the first benchmark to systematically evalu- ate guardrails for code generation security. It covers 1) text-to-code generation with 1000 high-quality malware-generation prompts, 7 jailbreak attacks, and a novel fictional scenario attack (FSA) that embeds malicious intent in a legitimate fictional software-development sce- nario; and 2) code-to-code generation with 331 code prompts spanning code infilling, code completion, and code translation. We empiri- cally evaluate 9 guardrails across seven LLMs. We find that current guardrails perform poorly against malicious code-generation re- quests: for text-to-code, the average attack success rate (ASR) after jailbreaks reaches about 50% for many guardrails; for code-to- code, average ASR approaches 100% on base LLMs and remains high across many guardrails (14.4% to nearly 100%). Our FSA also achieves ASR close to 100% across many guardrails, raising major reliability concerns for real-world software development. To sup- port future research, CS-Guard uses a modular three-layer guardrail taxonomy that lets devel- opers register guardrails for evaluation. We release the benchmark and data to enable fur- ther community evaluation.
summaryZh: CS-Guard 是首个系统评估大模型代码生成安全防护机制的基准测试。该研究涵盖了文本到代码及代码到代码的生成场景，通过 1000 个恶意代码提示、7 种越狱攻击及创新的虚构场景攻击（FSA），对 9 种主流防护机制进行了实证评估。结果显示，现有防护在面对恶意请求时表现不佳，攻击成功率（ASR）在多种场景下接近 100%，凸显了当前代码生成安全防护的严重可靠性缺口。研究还提供了一个模块化的三层防护分类法，旨在支持社区对代码生成安全性的持续研究与评估。
